usa.explanation: "USA" means "the USA". To say where someone lives, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i USA" (I live in the USA). Danes say the three letters one by one: "u", "es", "a".

uselvisk.explanation: "Uselvisk" means "unselfish". It is built from "u-" (un-) and "selvisk" (selfish).

usikker.explanation: "Usikker" means "unsure". When you say something is not safe, it means "unsafe": "en usikker bro" (an unsafe bridge).

uskadt.explanation: "Uskadt" means "unhurt". When you talk about a thing after a storm or an accident, it means "undamaged": "Huset er uskadt" (The house is undamaged).

uskarp.explanation: "Uskarp" means "blurry". It is built from "u-" (not) and "skarp" (sharp).

uskyld.explanation: "En uskyld" means "innocence". When you talk about a child's lack of experience of the world, use it for that too: "barnets uskyld" (the child's innocence).

uskyldig.explanation: "Uskyldig" means "innocent". When you describe a joke that is meant harmlessly, use it too: "Det er en uskyldig joke" (It is an innocent joke).

ustabil.explanation: "Ustabil" means "unstable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "stabil" (stable). To describe an internet connection that keeps failing, say: "Forbindelsen er ustabil" (The connection is unstable).

usund.explanation: "Usund" means "unhealthy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "sund" (healthy). To say a habit is bad for you, say: "Rygning er usundt" (Smoking is unhealthy).

usympatisk.explanation: "Usympatisk" means "unlikeable". English speakers may expect it to mean "unsympathetic", but it does not. To say someone feels for others, use "medfølende" (compassionate): "Hun er medfølende" (She is compassionate).

usynlig.explanation: "Usynlig" means "invisible". To say you can see something, use "synlig" (visible): "Stjernen er synlig" (The star is visible).

usædvanlig.explanation: "Usædvanlig" means "unusual". It is built from "u-" (not) and "sædvanlig" (usual).

utaknemmelig.explanation: "Utaknemmelig" means "ungrateful". When you describe a job that brings little reward, it means "thankless": "en utaknemmelig opgave" (a thankless task).

utallige.explanation: "Utallige" means "countless". When you talk about more than one thing, put it before the plural noun: "utallige stjerner" (countless stars).

utilfreds.explanation: "Utilfreds" means "dissatisfied". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tilfreds" (satisfied). To say what you are dissatisfied with, add "med" (with): "utilfreds med lønnen" (dissatisfied with the pay).

utilfredshed.explanation: "En utilfredshed" means "dissatisfaction". It is the noun for the adjective "utilfreds" (dissatisfied). To say what you are dissatisfied with, add "med" (with): "utilfredshed med servicen" (dissatisfaction with the service).

utilstrækkelig.explanation: "Utilstrækkelig" means "inadequate". When you describe a person who feels not good enough, it describes that person too: "Jeg føler mig utilstrækkelig" (I feel inadequate).

utro.explanation: "Utro" means "unfaithful". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tro" (true). To name the person who is betrayed, add "mod" (toward): "Han har været utro mod hende" (He has been unfaithful to her).

utrolig.explanation: "Utrolig" means "unbelievable". It is built from "at tro" (to believe) and "u-" (not). To react to surprising news, say: "Det er utroligt!" (That is unbelievable!).

utroligt.explanation: "Utroligt" means "incredibly". It comes from the adjective "utrolig" (unbelievable). To make an adjective stronger, put it before the adjective: "Det er utroligt varmt i dag" (It is incredibly hot today).

utydelig.explanation: "Utydelig" means "unclear". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tydelig" (clear). To describe handwriting that is hard to read, say: "utydelig skrift" (unclear handwriting).

utålmodig.explanation: "Utålmodig" means "impatient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tålmodig" (patient). To tell someone to wait, say: "Vær ikke så utålmodig!" (Do not be so impatient!).

utålmodighed.explanation: "En utålmodighed" means "impatience". It is the noun for the adjective "utålmodig" (impatient). To say how someone waited, use "med" (with): "Hun ventede med utålmodighed" (She waited with impatience).

uundgåelig.explanation: "Uundgåelig" means "unavoidable". To say something will happen anyway, say: "Forsinkelser er uundgåelige" (Delays are unavoidable).

uundværlig.explanation: "Uundværlig" means "indispensable". It comes from "at undvære" (to do without). To say you cannot do without your phone, say: "Min telefon er uundværlig" (My phone is indispensable).

uvant.explanation: "Uvant" means "unfamiliar". It is built from "u-" (not) and "vant" (used to). To say what you are not used to, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uvant med kulden" (I am not used to the cold).

uvedkommende.explanation: "Uvedkommende" means "unauthorized". When you say a question has nothing to do with the matter, it means "irrelevant": "et uvedkommende spørgsmål" (an irrelevant question). To keep people out of a place, a sign says: "Adgang forbudt for uvedkommende" (No entry for unauthorized persons).

uvenlig.explanation: "Uvenlig" means "unfriendly". It is built from "u-" (not) and "venlig" (friendly). To name the person who receives the unfriendly behavior, add "mod" (toward): "Hun var uvenlig mod mig" (She was unfriendly to me).

uventet.explanation: "Uventet" means "unexpected". To say something came as a surprise, put it after the verb: "Det kom helt uventet" (It came completely unexpectedly).

uvidende.explanation: "Uvidende" means "unaware". It is built from "u-" (not) and "at vide" (to know). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "Jeg er uvidende om reglerne" (I am unaware of the rules).

uvidenhed.explanation: "En uvidenhed" means "ignorance". It is the noun for the adjective "uvidende" (unaware). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "uvidenhed om reglerne" (ignorance of the rules).

uærlig.explanation: "Uærlig" means "dishonest". It is built from "u-" (not) and "ærlig" (honest).

at vaccinere.explanation: "At vaccinere" means "to vaccinate". To name the disease, add "mod" (against): "vaccinere mod influenza" (vaccinate against the flu). To say you are the person getting the shot, use "at lade sig vaccinere" (to let yourself be vaccinated): "Jeg lader mig vaccinere" (I am getting vaccinated).

at vade.explanation: "At vade" means "to wade". To say you walk out into the sea, add "ud i" (out into): "Vi vader ud i havet" (We wade out into the sea). To say someone is very rich, use "i penge" (in money): "Hun vader i penge" (She is rolling in money).

at vakle.explanation: "At vakle" means "to wobble / waver". To say a tired person walks unsteadily, use it for "to wobble": "Han vakler hjem" (He wobbles home). To say a decision is not firm, use it for "to waver": "Hans beslutning vakler" (His decision is wavering).

at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water". It comes from "vand" (water). To say you give animals water to drink, use it for them too: "at vande hestene" (to water the horses).

at vandre.explanation: "At vandre" means "to wander / hike". To say you go on foot for a long time in nature, use it for "to hike": "Vi vandrer langs kysten" (We hike along the coast). To say you walk around without hurry or goal, use it for "to wander": "Han vandrede rundt i byen" (He wandered around town).

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last". To say how long something goes on, add the length of time: "Filmen varer to timer" (The movie lasts two hours).

at variere.explanation: "At variere" means "to vary". To say something is not always the same, use it alone: "Prisen varierer" (The price varies). To say you change something on purpose, name the thing after it: "Jeg varierer menuen" (I vary the menu).

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash". To say you wash an object, name it after the verb: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car). To say you wash yourself, use "at vaske sig" (to wash oneself): "Jeg vasker mig" (I wash myself). To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?)

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor". In this phrase, "gulv" has no article: "Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen" (We mop the floor on Saturdays). To wipe up one spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up): "Jeg tørrer mælken op" (I wipe up the milk).

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes". To ask whose turn it is, say: "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?) Do not mix it up with "at vaske" (to wash). To say you wash a car, say: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash (oneself)". When you talk about another person, "sig" stays the same: "Han vasker sig" (He washes himself). To wash something else, use "at vaske" (to wash) and name the thing: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry". Literally, it is "to wash clothes". To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Jeg vasker op" (I do the dishes).

at vedkende sig.explanation: "At vedkende sig" means "to acknowledge". The word "sig" always goes with it. To name what you acknowledge, put it after "sig": "Han vedkender sig sin fejl" (He acknowledges his mistake).

at vedligeholde.explanation: "At vedligeholde" means "to maintain". To say you keep a house in good shape, say: "Vi vedligeholder huset" (We maintain the house). To say someone claims something, use "at hævde" (to claim): "Hun hævder, at det er sandt" (She claims that it is true).

at vedlægge.explanation: "At vedlægge" means "to enclose". It is built from "ved" (by) and "at lægge" (to put). To say you put a document in with an email, name it after the verb: "Jeg vedlægger kvitteringen" (I enclose the receipt).

at vedrøre.explanation: "At vedrøre" means "to concern". To say a matter affects someone, put the person after the verb: "Sagen vedrører dig" (The matter concerns you). To start the subject of an email, use "Vedrørende" (Regarding), a form of this word: "Vedrørende din ansøgning" (Regarding your application).

at vedtage.explanation: "At vedtage" means "to pass (a law) / adopt". "Folketinget" is the Danish parliament. To say it made a law official, say: "Folketinget vedtog loven" (Parliament passed the law).

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". To say how heavy you are, use the verb with a number: "Jeg vejer 70 kilo" (I weigh 70 kilos). To weigh an object on a scale, name the object after the verb: "Jeg vejer pakken" (I weigh the package).

at vejlede.explanation: "At vejlede" means "to guide / advise". It is built from "vej" (way) and "at lede" (to lead). To say someone helped you choose, say: "Hun vejledte mig i valget" (She advised me on the choice).

at veksle.explanation: "At veksle" means "to exchange (money)". To ask someone to break a big bill into smaller ones, say: "Kan du veksle en hundredkroneseddel?" (Can you break a hundred-krone bill?)

at velsigne.explanation: "At velsigne" means "to bless". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at signe" (to bless). To wish someone God's blessing, say: "Gud velsigne dig" (God bless you).

at vende.explanation: "At vende" means "to turn". To turn something over, name it after the verb: "Jeg vender kortet" (I turn the card over). To turn in a direction, use "at dreje" (to turn): "Drej til venstre" (Turn left).

at vende sig.explanation: "At vende sig" means "to turn around". To say someone turns their own body, say: "Han vendte sig og smilede" (He turned around and smiled). Do not mix it up with "at vænne sig til" (to get used to). To say you are getting used to something, say: "Jeg vænner mig til kulden" (I am getting used to the cold).

at vende tilbage.explanation: "At vende tilbage" means "to return". To say you come back to a topic in a talk, add "til" (to): "Lad os vende tilbage til spørgsmålet" (Let us return to the question). To say you will answer someone later, say: "Jeg vender tilbage til dig" (I will get back to you).

at vente.explanation: "At vente" means "to wait". To say what you wait for, add "på" (for): "Jeg venter på bussen" (I am waiting for the bus). To say a woman is pregnant, use it for "to expect": "Hun venter barn" (She is expecting a baby).

at vente på.explanation: "At vente på" means "to wait for". To ask who someone is waiting for, keep "på" (for) at the end of the question: "Hvem venter du på?" (Who are you waiting for?)

at verificere.explanation: "At verificere" means "to verify". To say you prove who you are, say: "at verificere sin identitet" (to verify your identity).

at vide.explanation: "At vide" means "to know (a fact)". To say you do not know something, say: "Jeg ved det ikke" (I do not know). To say you know a person, use "at kende" (to know someone): "Jeg kender Anna" (I know Anna).

at videreføre.explanation: "At videreføre" means "to continue". It is built from "videre" (onward) and "at føre" (to carry). To say you carry on something others began, name it after the verb: "De viderefører traditionen" (They carry on the tradition). To say you keep on doing something, use "at fortsætte" (to continue): "Jeg fortsætter med at læse" (I keep on reading).

at videregive.explanation: "At videregive" means "to pass on". It is built from "videre" (onward) and "at give" (to give). To say you pass a message on, say: "Jeg videregiver beskeden til chefen" (I pass the message on to the boss).

at vidne.explanation: "At vidne" means "to testify". To name the person who testifies, use "et vidne" (a witness): "Hun er et vidne" (She is a witness). To say something shows a quality, add "om" (about): "Resultatet vidner om hårdt arbejde" (The result shows hard work).

at vifte.explanation: "At vifte" means "to wave". To wave something back and forth, add "med" (with): "Han vifter med en avis" (He waves a newspaper). To wave to a person, use "at vinke" (to wave to someone): "Han vinkede til mig" (He waved to me). To name a fan, use the noun "en vifte" (a fan): "Jeg tænder for viften" (I turn on the fan).

at ville.explanation: "At ville" means "to want to / will". To say you want something, say: "Jeg vil have en kop kaffe" (I want a cup of coffee). To make it polite, add "gerne" (gladly): "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like a cup of coffee). To say you have to do something, use "skal" (have to): "Jeg skal gå" (I have to go).

at vinde.explanation: "At vinde" means "to win". To say someone won a contest, name it after the verb: "Hun vandt konkurrencen" (She won the competition). The person who wins is "en vinder" (a winner).

at vinke.explanation: "At vinke" means "to wave". To say who you wave at, add "til" (to): "Han vinkede til mig" (He waved to me). To say you wave goodbye, add "farvel" (goodbye): "Han vinkede farvel" (He waved goodbye).

at vippe.explanation: "At vippe" means "to tip / rock". To tell a child to stop rocking a chair, say: "Vip ikke med stolen!" (Do not rock the chair!) To name the playground seesaw, use the noun "en vippe" (a seesaw): "Børnene leger på vippen" (The children play on the seesaw).

at virke.explanation: "At virke" means "to work / seem". To say a machine functions, use it for "to work": "Bilen virker ikke" (The car does not work). To say someone gives a certain impression, use it for "to seem": "Han virker træt" (He seems tired).

at vise.explanation: "At vise" means "to show". To show a thing, name it after the verb: "Jeg viser billedet" (I show the picture). To show something to a person, put the person right after the verb, with no "til" (to): "Hun viser mig bogen" (She shows me the book).

at vise sig.explanation: "At vise sig" means "to turn out". To say what a person turned out to be, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Hun viste sig at være meget flink" (She turned out to be very nice).

at visne.explanation: "At visne" means "to wither". To say a plant is slowly dying, add "hen" (away): "Planten visner hen" (The plant is withering away).

at visualisere.explanation: "At visualisere" means "to visualize". To say you picture something in your mind, say: "Jeg kan visualisere huset" (I can visualize the house). To say you show data as a graph, say: "at visualisere data" (to visualize data).

at vokse.explanation: "At vokse" means "to grow". To say someone or something gets bigger, say: "Børn vokser hurtigt" (Children grow fast). To say where you spent your childhood, use "at vokse op" (to grow up): "Jeg voksede op i Odense" (I grew up in Odense). To grow tomatoes, use "at dyrke" (to cultivate): "Jeg dyrker tomater" (I grow tomatoes).

at vokse op.explanation: "At vokse op" means "to grow up". It is built from "at vokse" (to grow) and "op" (up). To say where you spent your childhood, say: "Jeg voksede op i Odense" (I grew up in Odense). Without "op", "at vokse" means "to grow", as in "Træet vokser hurtigt" (The tree grows quickly).

at vove.explanation: "At vove" means "to dare". To say you dare to do something, you can also use "at turde" (to dare): "Jeg tør ikke" (I do not dare).

at vride.explanation: "At vride" means "to twist / wring". To squeeze water out of a cloth, name the cloth: "Jeg vrider håndklædet" (I wring the towel). To say someone twists in pain, add "sig" (oneself): "Han vred sig af smerte" (He writhed in pain).

at vrimle.explanation: "At vrimle" means "to swarm / teem". To say what a place is full of, add "med" (with): "Gaden vrimler med mennesker" (The street teems with people).

at vurdere.explanation: "At vurdere" means "to evaluate". To say an expert names a value for a house, say: "Huset bliver vurderet til tre millioner" (The house is valued at three million).

at vågne.explanation: "At vågne" means "to wake up". To say you woke up early, say: "Jeg vågnede tidligt" (I woke up early). When someone else wakes you, use "at vække" (to wake someone): "Min mor vækker mig" (My mother wakes me).

at vågne op.explanation: "At vågne op" means "to wake up". It is built from "at vågne" (to wake up) and "op" (up). To say you woke in the night, say: "Jeg vågnede op midt om natten" (I woke up in the middle of the night).

at vædde.explanation: "At vædde" means "to bet". To name the event you bet on, use "på" (on): "Vi vædder på vejret" (We bet on the weather).

at vække.explanation: "At vække" means "to wake (someone)". To say you wake another person, name the person: "Jeg vækker børnene" (I wake the children). To say you wake up yourself, use "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede tidligt" (I woke up early).

at vælge.explanation: "At vælge" means "to choose". The noun "et valg" has two meanings. To say a decision is yours, use it for "a choice": "Det er dit valg" (It is your choice). To say people vote, use it for "an election": "Der er valg i dag" (There is an election today).

at vælte.explanation: "At vælte" means "to knock over / tip over". To say you knock something over, name it: "Jeg vælter koppen" (I knock over the cup). To say something goes over by itself, leave out the thing you knocked: "Træet væltede" (The tree fell over).

at vænne sig af med.explanation: "At vænne sig af med" means "to get out of the habit of". To say what you stopped doing, add "at" (to) and the verb: "Han vænnede sig af med at ryge" (He got out of the habit of smoking). To say you get used to something, use "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg vænner mig til kulden" (I am getting used to the cold).

at vænne sig til.explanation: "At vænne sig til" means "to get used to". To say you are already used to something, use "vant til" (used to): "Jeg er vant til kulden" (I am used to the cold).

at værdsætte.explanation: "At værdsætte" means "to appreciate". It is built from "værd" (worth) and "at sætte" (to set). To say you are glad of someone's help, say: "Jeg værdsætter din hjælp" (I appreciate your help). To say something rises in value, use "at stige i værdi" (to rise in value): "Huset stiger i værdi" (The house is rising in value).

at være.explanation: "At være" means "to be". To say how someone feels, use the form "er" (am, is, are): "Jeg er glad" (I am happy). The form "er" is the same for every person: "han er" (he is), "vi er" (we are).

at være bange for.explanation: "At være bange for" means "to be afraid of". To say what action you fear, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg er bange for at falde" (I am afraid of falling).

at være enig.explanation: "At være enig" means "to agree". Literally, it is "to be in agreement". To say who you agree with, add "med" (with): "Jeg er enig med dig" (I agree with you). To say what you agree with, add "i" (in): "Jeg er enig i planen" (I agree with the plan).

at være i tvivl.explanation: "At være i tvivl" means "to be in doubt". To name the subject of your doubt, add "om" (about): "Jeg er i tvivl om svaret" (I am in doubt about the answer).

at være kærester.explanation: "At være kærester" means "to be dating". One person in the couple is "en kæreste" (a boyfriend or girlfriend): "Hun er min kæreste" (She is my girlfriend).

at være med.explanation: "At være med" means "to take part / be in on it". To invite someone to join, ask: "Er du med?" (Are you in?) To say you do not follow what is being said, say: "Jeg er ikke helt med" (I am not quite following).

at være nødt til.explanation: "At være nødt til" means "to have to". To say you have no other choice, say: "Jeg er nødt til at gå nu" (I have to go now). To say what you are going to do, use "skal" (am going to): "Jeg skal på arbejde" (I am going to work).

at være oppe at køre.explanation: "At være oppe at køre" means "to be worked up". To say someone is tense before an event, say: "Hun var helt oppe at køre før brylluppet" (She was all worked up before the wedding).

at være på bar bund.explanation: "At være på bar bund" means "to be at a total loss". Literally, it is "to be on bare bottom". The word "bar" (bare) also appears in "bare fødder" (bare feet).

at være på herrens mark.explanation: "At være på Herrens mark" means "to be completely lost". Literally, it is "to be on the Lord's field". To tell someone they are wrong, say: "Der er du helt på Herrens mark" (You are completely off there).

related.da: at være helt ude at svømme
related.en: to be out of your depth
to be on the right track

at være på vej.explanation: "At være på vej" means "to be on one's way". To say where you are heading, add the place: "Jeg er på vej hjem" (I am on my way home). To name a city you are heading to, add "til" (to): "Han er på vej til Aarhus" (He is on his way to Aarhus).

at være syg.explanation: "At være syg" means "to be sick". To say you are getting sick, use "at blive syg" (to become sick): "Jeg bliver syg" (I am getting sick).
